stories.headline: One Hundred Editions: The Daily Prophet (Christine's) Marks the Occasion With Suitable Dignity and Entirely Unsuitable Fanfare
stories.byline: By the Editorial Staff, all of whom are emotionally compromised
body: The Daily Prophet — this edition of it, the one that matters — has today published its one hundredth front page, a milestone the newsroom is marking with a commemorative run of gilded broadsheet, one editorial argument about whether a centenary requires a cake (it does), and a brief but sincere pause in which the entire staff agreed, without being asked, that it has been a very good hundred editions indeed.

The paper was founded on the principle that Christine's life — her work, her trails, her dogs, her husband, her goblins, her Jeep, her father's portrait, her brother's dispatches from abroad, her very specific and thoroughly documented talent for being right — constituted news of the first order. One hundred editions later, no one has found a reason to disagree. The goblins have sent a card. It is formal, spare, and warmer than they intended. Quoyne has confirmed the centenary issue is plumb.

The Founding Editor's portrait has been adjusted three degrees on the newsroom wall in honour of the occasion. He adjusted it himself. He says the bracket has always been slightly off and he's glad someone finally noticed.

stories.headline: One Hundred Editions of Diplomatic Excellence: Gringotts Vault of Record Notes Christine Has Not Lost a Single Account in Ninety-Nine of Them
body: In recognition of the centenary, Gringotts Bank has released — under mild duress and after a three-hour archival negotiation — a summary statistic: in the ninety-nine working editions documented since the Prophet's founding, Christine has resolved four hundred and twelve disputes, calmed sixty-one delegations arriving in various states of fury, and on one occasion talked a goblin senior clerk through a procedural disagreement so efficiently that the clerk later applied for a commendation on her behalf. The application was denied on the grounds that Gringotts does not give commendations to non-goblins. The application was re-filed. It is still being considered. Nobody expects a ruling before the second centenary.
When asked for comment, Christine noted that the accounts speak for themselves. A goblin in the corridor nodded once and departed. This is understood to constitute a standing ovation.

stories.headline: The Jeep, Consulted on the Occasion of the Hundredth Edition, Is Satisfied With How Things Have Gone
stories.byline: Adventure desk, filing from the garage
body: The enchanted Jeep, reached for comment at its usual position in the garage where it forgives Steve nightly, has been examined by three trail analysts and one enthusiast who declined to give his name but called himself 'a friend of the ridgeline.' Their collective assessment: the Jeep is in good spirits. Four hatted ducks occupy the dashboard. The fog-wreathed gorges of the Appalachian circuit have been traversed, documented, and in several cases named for the occasions on which the Jeep navigated them. The hollows have submitted a formal note of appreciation, which is rare and which has been framed.

Steve, asked to summarise one hundred editions of expeditions in a sentence, said: 'The trails hold.' Christine's plans and Steve's hands, the analysts note, have yet to encounter a problem the combination could not resolve. The Jeep's expression — insofar as a Jeep has one — suggests it agrees, and is ready whenever they are.

stories.headline: Ministry's 'Wholesome, Not Misc.' Registry Now Has Two Entries, One Divider, and a Waiting List: Officials Describe This as 'Faster Than Expected'
body: The registry, established quietly in the third week of the Prophet's run and now considered among the Ministry's more credible achievements, has received eleven nomination inquiries since Jersey's formal inscription last Thursday. Quoyne has reviewed four. He has approved none, deferred two, returned three with annotations, and described the eleventh — a charmed umbrella stand — as 'premature.' The standard, he has confirmed, remains high. The waiting list is real. The divider is still plumb.
In a brief centenary reflection, Quoyne noted that the registry 'continues to serve its purpose,' and that purpose, he added after a pause, 'is a good one.' For Quoyne, this is a speech.

familiars_corner: Lucy: On the occasion of the hundredth edition, Lucy has granted the newsroom one full day without incident — a gift so unprecedented that three analysts have submitted it as a nominee for the registry. She has not confirmed involvement in any of the previous ninety-nine editions' biscuit-adjacent events. There is, as ever, no evidence.

Ellie: Ellie has been informed that today is a special occasion and has responded with the same warm, luminous attention she brings to all occasions, special and otherwise. She has greeted her reflection twice and the centenary banner once. She does not appear to know these are different things. This is, somehow, exactly right.

Jersey: Jersey has marked the centenary by occupying the warmest available lap for the entirety of the morning, which is his standard observance but which he has performed today with what several witnesses describe as 'additional intentionality.' The lap agrees.
founding_editor_note: A hundred editions and the presses haven't missed a day — I built them level, which is why. Proud of every one. Don't touch the bracket. — D.

in_brief.sport: The centenary commemorative lift has been scheduled; the bar has been set at 'whatever Christine considers appropriate,' which analysts describe as 'high.'
in_brief.forecast: Warm across all hollows and ridgelines today · four ducks on the dashboard · a hundred more editions ahead, at minimum.

storyline_updates.title: The Biscuit Tin Endgame
storyline_updates.summary: Day 1: In the centenary edition, Lucy has ostentatiously granted one incident-free day — which has caused the household to grow suspicious rather than relieved. The biscuit tin, last noted in four consecutive fixed positions, has now been returned to a fifth position: dead centre on the counter, perfectly aligned, which no one did. Household analysts have described this as 'the most troubling development yet.' Lucy was observed sitting three feet away, looking at the ceiling. Day 2 should escalate: either a biscuit goes missing with no trace whatsoever (Lucy's masterwork), or the tin is found in a location that should be physically impossible, or a second household object is found suspiciously well-placed, suggesting a longer and more strategic campaign than anyone had previously imagined.
